attributes.body_ja:
「とも」は終助詞（しゅうじょし）、接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）、または副助詞（ふくじょし）として使（つか）われることがある助詞（じょし）です。助詞（じょし）の種類（しゅるい）が何（なに）になるかは、一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）う語（ご）によって変（か）わります。助詞（じょし）の種類（しゅるい）が変わっても、意味（いみ）はほとんど同（おな）じです。「とも」は基本的（きほんてき）に「たとえ (A) でも」という意味（いみ）で使（つか）われ、(A) という状況（じょうきょう）でも、(B) は変（か）わらないことを表（あらわ）します。

接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）として使（つか）う場合（ばあい）、助動詞（じょどうし）の「う」や「よう」が付（つ）く動詞（どうし）、またはイ形容詞（けいようし）の連用形（れんようけい）の後（あと）に置（お）かれます。

副助詞（ふくじょし）として使（つか）う場合（ばあい）、イ形容詞（けいようし）の連用形（れんようけい）や一部（いちぶ）の副詞（ふくし）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。ただし、副詞（ふくし）と使（つか）うパターンはあまり多（おお）くないので、実際（じっさい）にネイティブが使（つか）っているのを見（み）た表現（ひょうげん）だけを使（つか）うのがおすすめです。
attributes.body:
とも is a particle that can be used either as a sentence-ending particle, conjunction particle, or adverbial particle. Despite this, the meanings are often interchangeable, and it depends mostly on what type of word they are grouped with as to which type of particle it is. Common interpretations of とも in almost any situation are 'even if (A)', or 'no matter if (A)', and it will basically always simply highlight that 'in spite of (A), still (B)'.

As a conjunction particle, とも will be paired with any words that are followed by the auxiliary verbs う, or よう, or after い-Adjectives in their conjunctive form.

The adverbial particle usage only appears after い-Adjectives in their conjunctive form, and a select number of adverbs. It is recommended not to use this structure after adverbs unless you have already seen it used this way in native material.

にしても and とも both express 'even if', but differ in formality and structure. にしても follows the plain, non-past form and is more common in daily language, e.g. どこに行くにしても ('No matter where you go'). とも follows the volitional form and is more formal and emphatic, often found in set expressions like 何があろうとも ('No matter what happens').

first_relatable.title: にしても
first_relatable.meaning: Even though, Even if, Even when, Also

attributes.body: Both express strong contrary hypotheticals, similar to 'Even if (A), still (B)'. たとえ〜ても is less formal and more common in speech, e.g. たとえ一人でも、ちゃんとやる 'Even if it's just me, I'll do it right.' とも is more literary and formal, and takes the volitional form, e.g. 死のうとも構わない 'Even if I die, I don't mind.'

first_relatable.title: たとえ〜ても
first_relatable.meaning: Even if…is the case, Supposing that

attributes.body: どうしても and とも both express the meaning of 'even if' or 'no matter', but differ in formality and placement. どうしても comes at the beginning of a sentence to emphasize determination, as in どうしても勝ちたい ('I want to win no matter what'). とも is a verb ending, often more formal or literary than ても. For example, 彼女が何と言おうとも ('No matter what she says') is equivalent in meaning to 彼女が何と言っても, but more formal.

Both mean even if or no matter if. とも states a single condition in a slightly formal style, as in 雨が降ろうとも行く (I’ll go even if it rains). ようが～まいが is more emphatic, presenting contrasting alternatives, as in 雨が降ろうが降るまいが行く (I’ll go whether it rains or not).

first_relatable.meaning: Even if, No matter what, Whether or not, [Emphatic], Volitional + が
